## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vaṭṭakajātaka* (Ja 118) is a birth story found in the *Ekanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877]. Its opening verse begins with the phrase *Nācintayanto puriso* ("The thoughtless man") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. According to its commentary (*nidāna*), the Buddha recounted the narrative while dwelling at Jetavana in connection with the son of the Over-Treasurer (Uttaraseṭṭhiputta) of Sāvatthī, a wealthy merchant whose wife gave birth to a meritorious being descending from the realm of Brahmā deities [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. The title is listed among other canonical Jātaka verses in modern anthologies [Anandajoti 2010].
While DharmaNexus identifies no significant internal Pali text reuse or cross-language matches above its threshold [DharmaNexus], SuttaCentral records a full parallel to the narrative in the Sanskrit Mahāvastu under the title *The Jātaka of the Bird* (Mvu 56) [SuttaCentral]. This text should not be confused with other Jātakas bearing the same name, particularly the well-known *Vaṭṭakajātaka* (Ja 35), which concerns a baby quail's act of truth holding back a forest fire [Appleton 2010; Söhnen-Thieme], or the *Vaṭṭakajātaka* of the higher nipātas (Ja 394) [Fausböll 1883].
